title: Retrospective Modals: Should Have, Could Have, Needn't Have
grammarTitle: Retrospective Modals — Past Advice, Regret & Criticism
grammarNote: Ретроспективные модальные глаголы (should have, could have, might have, needn't have) описывают прошлые ситуации с позиции настоящего: что нужно было, можно было, не нужно было сделать. Это грамматика сожаления, критики, нереализованных возможностей и ненужных действий.

grammarTable.subject: should have + pp
grammarTable.example: "You should have called." (you didn't — this was wrong/a mistake)

grammarTable.subject: shouldn't have + pp
grammarTable.example: "You shouldn't have eaten so much." (you did — this was a mistake)

grammarTable.subject: could have + pp
grammarTable.example: "She could have applied earlier." (option existed, not taken)

grammarTable.subject: might have + pp
grammarTable.example: "He might have called, but I was busy." (uncertain/possible)

grammarTable.subject: needn't have + pp
grammarTable.example: "You needn't have bought so much food." (you did — but it wasn't needed)

grammarTable.subject: ought to have + pp
grammarTable.example: "She ought to have checked the report." (stronger criticism)

grammarExtra.title: Should have vs could have: judgement vs observation

rows.form: should have = JUDGEMENT — it was wrong not to
rows.example: "She should have applied." = It was wrong that she didn't. Judgement.
"She could have applied." = The option was there. Observation, not criticism.
"You could have told me earlier." (observation: you had the option) ✅
"You should have told me earlier." (judgement: it was wrong that you didn't) ✅
"She could have won — she was the strongest competitor." (had the ability) ✅

grammarExtra.title: Needn't have vs didn't need to

rows.form: needn't have + pp = DID it, was unnecessary
rows.example: "I needn't have WORRIED — it went fine." (I worried, but I didn't need to.) ✅

rows.form: didn't need to + base = DIDN'T do it (normal)
rows.example: "I didn't need to worry — I knew it would be fine." (So I didn't worry.) ✅

rows.form: The KEY difference: did the action happen?
rows.example: "Needn't have done" = DID do it (but wasted effort). "Didn't need to" = DIDN'T do it. ✅
"She needn't have prepared extra slides." (she prepared them — unnecessarily) vs "She didn't need to prepare extra slides." (so she didn't) ✅

grammarExtra.title: Ought to have — stronger than should have

rows.form: ought to have + pp = stronger moral obligation
rows.example: "She ought to have disclosed the conflict of interest." (clear moral failure) ✅

rows.form: Similar to should have but more formal
rows.example: "You ought to have checked." ≈ "You should have checked." — more formal/literary ✅
"They ought to have been informed earlier." (legal/ethical weight) ✅

grammarExtra.title: Was able to vs could have — past ability and opportunity

rows.form: was/were able to = did manage (specific achievement)
rows.example: "She was able to finish on time." (she managed it — achievement) ✅

rows.form: could + base form = general ability in past
rows.example: "She could speak Kazakh fluently at 12." (general ability, not specific event) ✅

rows.form: could have + pp = had ability but didn't use it
rows.example: "She could have finished earlier, but chose not to." (had the ability — didn't use it) ✅
"He couldn't solve the problem." (general inability at that time) ✅
✅ "I should have GONE." — past participle of "go" = "gone." ✅
✅ "She needn't have WORRIED." — needn't have + pp, no "to." ✅
✅ "He could have AVOIDED it." — past participle required. ✅

rows.form: ✗ Confusing could have (observation) with should have (judgement)
rows.example: "You could have called." (option existed) ≠ "You should have called." (it was wrong that you didn't) ✅

grammarTip:
Retrospective Modals:

should have + pp → criticism/regret (didn't do)
"You SHOULD HAVE told me." (you didn't — mistake)

shouldn't have + pp → criticism (did do)
"You SHOULDN'T HAVE said that." (you said — mistake)

could have + pp → opportunity existed but unused
"She COULD HAVE applied." (option was there)

needn't have + pp → done but unnecessary
"You NEEDN'T HAVE bought so much." (you did, wasted effort)

ought to have + pp → stronger should have
"They OUGHT TO HAVE been informed."

was able to = managed to do (specific achievement)
could have + pp = had ability but didn't use it

⚠️ Errors:
✗ should have went → ✅ should have GONE
✗ needn't have to → ✅ needn't have (no 'to')
✗ could have avoid → ✅ could have AVOIDED

exercises.instruction: Should have — criticism of action not done.
exercises.hint: "should have LEFT" = retrospective criticism. She didn't leave earlier — and she should have. ✅

exercises.instruction: Shouldn't have — criticism of action done.
exercises.text: "He told everyone the secret. He ___ (tell) anyone."
exercises.hint: "SHOULDN'T HAVE TOLD" — he told everyone; this was wrong. ✅

exercises.instruction: Could have vs should have — which is an OBSERVATION (not judgement)?
exercises.text: "She ___ applied for the scholarship. All the criteria were met."
opts: should have (judgement: she was wrong not to)
exercises.hint: "could have applied" = the option was available. Observation, not judgement. "Should have" = it was wrong not to. ✅

exercises.text: "We ___ (bring) so much food — there was already plenty."
exercises.hint: "We NEEDN'T HAVE BROUGHT so much food." = We did bring it, but it was unnecessary. ✅

exercises.instruction: Needn't have vs didn't need to. Choose.
exercises.text: "She prepared for ten hours, but the presentation was cancelled." →  She ___.
exercises.hint: "She NEEDN'T HAVE PREPARED." = She DID prepare (ten hours!) but it turned out to be unnecessary. ✅

exercises.instruction: Didn't need to vs needn't have.
exercises.text: "She knew it would be cancelled, so she ___."
opts: didn't need to prepare (so she didn't)
exercises.correct: didn't need to prepare (so she didn't)
exercises.hint: "didn't need to prepare" = so she didn't. (The action wasn't done.) ✅ vs "needn't have prepared" = she did but it was unnecessary. ✅

exercises.instruction: Ought to have — stronger moral obligation.
exercises.text: "The company ___ (disclose) the risks to investors. They didn't."
opts: Both should and ought to are correct
exercises.correct: Both should and ought to are correct
exercises.hint: "SHOULD HAVE DISCLOSED" ✅ / "OUGHT TO HAVE DISCLOSED" ✅ — both correct. "Ought to" = stronger moral/legal weight. ✅

exercises.instruction: Find the error and correct it.
exercises.text: "He should have went to see a doctor immediately."
exercises.hint: "He should have GONE to see a doctor." — "gone" = past participle of "go." Not "went" (past simple)! ✅

exercises.instruction: Was able to vs could have — specific achievement.
exercises.text: "Despite the deadline, she ___ finish the report on time." (she actually finished it)
exercises.hint: "was able to finish" = managed to do it (specific achievement). "Could have finished" would mean she had the ability but didn't use it. ✅

exercises.text: "He had all the resources but never wrote the novel. He ___ (write) it."
exercises.hint: "He COULD HAVE WRITTEN it." = had the opportunity/ability but didn't use it. Observation of unrealised potential. ✅

exercises.text: "You ___ (worry) so much — it all worked out fine!"
exercises.hint: "SHOULDN'T HAVE WORRIED" = criticises the worrying as a mistake. "NEEDN'T HAVE WORRIED" = the worry was done but was unnecessary. Both ✅ — different nuances. ✅

exercises.text: "They ___ have been warned before the meeting. Nobody told them."
exercises.hint: "They SHOULD HAVE BEEN WARNED." / "They OUGHT TO HAVE BEEN WARNED." ✅ (Both correct; ought to = slightly stronger moral weight.)

exercises.text: "She ___ (run) faster — she was in excellent shape. But she chose to pace herself."
exercises.hint: "COULD HAVE RUN faster." = had the ability but didn't use it (chose not to). ✅

exercises.instruction: Complex situation — which is most appropriate?
exercises.text: The meeting was rescheduled and nobody told Rustam. He drove across the city for nothing.
opts: "Rustam needn't have driven to the meeting."
"Rustam shouldn't have driven to the meeting."
"Rustam could have driven to the meeting."
"Rustam ought to have driven to the meeting."
exercises.correct: "Rustam needn't have driven to the meeting."
exercises.hint: "Rustam NEEDN'T HAVE DRIVEN." = he drove (did the action) but it turned out to be unnecessary (meeting cancelled). ✅

exercises.text: "She ___ (not / take) the job without reading the contract. It had terrible conditions."
exercises.hint: "She SHOULDN'T HAVE TAKEN the job." = she took it — this was a mistake. Criticism of past action that was done. ✅

exercises.instruction: Identify: what type of retrospective modal?
exercises.text: "We could have asked for more time. There was no reason to rush."
opts: Criticism: it was wrong not to ask
Observation: the option existed but wasn't taken
exercises.correct: Observation: the option existed but wasn't taken
exercises.hint: "could have asked" = observation that the option was available. Not criticism (should have), not unnecessary action (needn't have). ✅

opts: Criticism/regret — action NOT done; it was wrong not to
questions.correct: Criticism/regret — action NOT done; it was wrong not to
questions.hint: "should have + pp" = the action wasn't done and this was a mistake/regret. ✅

opts: The action was done but was unnecessary
It was wrong to do it
questions.correct: The action was done but was unnecessary
questions.hint: "needn't have + pp" = done, but it turned out to be unnecessary. ✅

opts: "should have" = judgement (wrong not to); "could have" = observation (option existed)
questions.correct: "should have" = judgement (wrong not to); "could have" = observation (option existed)

questions.text: "He ___ (not / say) that. It was very rude."
questions.hint: "He SHOULDN'T HAVE SAID that." = he said it — this was a mistake/rude. ✅

questions.text: "She didn't need to prepare vs she needn't have prepared." — difference:
opts: "Didn't need to" = didn't prepare (not necessary, so she didn't); "needn't have" = prepared but it was unnecessary
questions.correct: "Didn't need to" = didn't prepare (not necessary, so she didn't); "needn't have" = prepared but it was unnecessary
questions.hint: "didn't need to" = so didn't do. "needn't have" = did it but was wasted. ✅

opts: A stronger, more formal version of should have
questions.correct: A stronger, more formal version of should have
questions.hint: "ought to have + pp" = stronger/more formal retrospective criticism. ✅
✅ "She should have GONE." — past participle of "go" = "gone." Not "went." ✅

questions.text: "Was able to finish" vs "could have finished":
opts: "Was able to" = actually managed to do; "could have" = had ability but didn't use it
questions.correct: "Was able to" = actually managed to do; "could have" = had ability but didn't use it
questions.hint: "was able to finish" = she finished. "could have finished" = she had the ability but didn't. ✅

opts: "to" should be removed — needn't have + pp (no "to")
questions.correct: "to" should be removed — needn't have + pp (no "to")
questions.hint: ✅ "You needn't have WORRIED." — no "to" after "needn't have." ✅

questions.text: "You should have told me earlier." — vs "You could have told me earlier." — choose the JUDGEMENT:
questions.hint: "should have" = judgement (wrong not to tell). "could have" = observation (option existed). ✅

questions.text: "She needn't have prepared extra slides." — This implies:
opts: She prepared them, but the preparation was wasted
She had no ability to prepare
questions.correct: She prepared them, but the preparation was wasted
questions.hint: "needn't have prepared" = she did prepare (action done) but it turned out to be unnecessary. ✅
"ought to have" = strongest moral obligation retrospective. ✅
